narrative:
Cloudflare Public Bug Bounty (HackerOne, bug_bounty tier). Ran bucket-hunter Pass A (75 candidates generated, 14 found with all_users_read=true in acl JSON), secret-hunter Passes A+B+C against the cloudflare GH org, ownership-verifier on 4 assets (1 GH org → owned, 3 S3 buckets → unknown), and report-drafter for 1 high-severity leaked-credentials finding. Submitted to H1 as report #3738898.

Pass A of secret-hunter against the cloudflare org was the productive path this engagement. Trufflehog found 11 verified candidates; 9 were immediately identifiable as the EBI public tutorial Postgres database (hh-pgsql-public.ebi.ac.uk, deliberately public, used in Cloudflare Workers docs), and 2 were genuinely reportable: a Monday.com JWT and a Storyblok Access Token both hard-coded in cloudflare/moltworker (last pushed 2026-05-09). The 272 noseyparker findings from Pass C were all confirmed test fixtures in cloudflare-go — PEM keys in _test.go files, the well-known dummy API key 144c9defac04969c7bfad8efaa8ea194, and sequential-byte test vectors. NP produced zero net candidates.

The three S3 bucket ownership checks all returned unknown and, importantly, could never have returned otherwise. 'cloudflare-prod', 'cloudflare-backups', and 'backup-cloudflare' are generic brand-prefixed names that attract thousands of third-party GitHub hits from community users backing up their own Cloudflare configs. GH Check A consistently came back ambiguous (0 hits in cloudflare/* org, hundreds of hits in unrelated repos). Wayback word-boundary mode (already a live rule from the mercadolibre engagement) correctly returned 0 or inconclusive on all three. These bucket names are structurally unresolvable for this program — the bucket-hunter should skip them on future runs.

One ACL narration inconsistency deserves a note: the bucket-hunter summary.notes prose said 'perm_all_users_read=0 on all 14 hits means s3scanner confirmed list_bucket is ALLOWED', whereas the structured acl JSON field shows all_users_read=true on every candidate. The JSON is correct; the prose conflated s3scanner's numeric permission-code (0 = public/allowed) with a false reading of 'zero hits'. Downstream agents (report-drafter, human reviewer) should trust the structured acl object, not the prose narration. No rule can encode this in v1 schema, but it is worth noting for future bucket-hunter prompt edits.

For the next visit to this slug: the GH org is confirmed owned; skip re-verification. The EBI Postgres findings will reappear in cloudflare-docs on every future scan — once a platform outcome is recorded for report #3738898 (informative or otherwise), add hh-pgsql-public.ebi.ac.uk as a report_drafter.auto_info_filter entry. If revisiting for secrets, Pass A against the cloudflare org remains worthwhile (moltworker was the find); consider also scanning cloudflare-adjacent orgs (e.g., cloudflare-labs) if allowed under the policy cap. Bucket work is low-ROI: all 14 found buckets are unverifiable generics — skip unless a bucket appears with a non-brand-stem name that GH code search can pin to a cloudflare org repo.
